clue.text: Approaching in sportswear reveals flaws

indicators.note: the word in places the approaching piece inside the sportswear piece

parts.note: shorts are short trousers worn for sport
coming means approaching, drawing near

explanation.surface: Someone's choice of athletic kit as they draw near exposes their weaknesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcomings are defects or failings, so flaws is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Help check text of plot within trial

indicators.note: within places the plot word inside the trial word

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal trial
a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A legal case hinges on a story concealed inside the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to correct and prepare copy for publication as an assistant editor.

clue.text: Move mules — both stripped part of plant

indicators.note: stripped means losing the outer layer, so each of the two words loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone shifts stubborn animals, both of which have been shorn bare.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is the structure in a flower's ovary that becomes a seed after fertilisation.

clue.text: Flying beast got hermit agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A recluse got upset by some winged creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger moth is a brightly patterned moth, an insect that flies, and also a classic biplane.

clue.text: Old ox rising fine

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads the word upwards, so it is backwards

parts.note: a yak is a type of ox

explanation.surface: An elderly bull stands up and is said to be in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay means acceptable or satisfactory, just as fine does.

clue.text: Anxious in short time on river

parts.note: SEC is short for second, a short time
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Someone is nervous after spending only a moment on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means lacking confidence, uneasy or worried.

clue.text: Virtue of good people

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Moral goodness is presented as a quality belonging to decent folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace is a moral excellence or divine favour, a Christian quality like a virtue.

clue.text: Record start of diet? Count me out!

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the next word
out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieter logs the start of their regime and promptly opts out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count me out' reads as a refusal; 'out' rearranges COUNTME after D.
explanation.definitionFit: To document something is to record it in writing.

clue.text: Deny soldiers about to intercept aircraft

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

indicators.note: to intercept is to come in between, so the about letter goes into the aircraft

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: Troops refuse to stop a plane in mid-air.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject something is to refuse or turn it down, which is to deny it.

clue.text: Type of music depressed one singing

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling depressed
in slang an informer 'sings' to the police, and an informer is a grass

explanation.surface: A melancholy singer is presented as an example of a musical genre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singing' here is criminal slang for informing, and a GRASS is a British word for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluegrass is a style of American country music played on banjo, fiddle and guitar.

clue.text: Bad smell in street overhead

indicators.note: the bad smell is placed inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: AVE is short for avenue, a street
BO is body odour, a bad smell

explanation.surface: A stink hangs in the road, wafting up above people's heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overhead is located higher up, which is the sense of the adverb used here.

clue.text: Dull not having alcohol over bit of cereal

indicators.note: the dry piece goes over, covering on both sides, the cereal piece

parts.note: a dry event or person has no alcohol
an ear is the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant like wheat

explanation.surface: A teetotal breakfast is judged boring, with only cereal on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary describes something tedious and lifeless, a close synonym for dull.

clue.text: Plan escape needing to return after school

indicators.note: the reversed escape piece is placed after the school abbreviation
to return is to come back, so the escape word is read backwards

parts.note: to elude is to escape

explanation.surface: Someone plans a getaway that requires coming back once school finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or programme of intended events, so it means a plan.

clue.text: Material X subsumes fellow, oddly

indicators.note: to subsume is to take within, so the number holds the other letters

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of fellow

explanation.surface: A mysterious substance absorbs a man in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives F, L, O from fellow; these go inside TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Teflon is the trade name of a non-stick plastic coating, a material used on pans.

clue.text: Some paralytic or effectively keeled over showing savagery

indicators.note: keeled over means upturned, so in a down clue the letters read upwards
some of the words means a run of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: A drunk effectively collapses, showing violent behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paralytic' is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferocity is fierce violence or cruelty, the same as savagery.

clue.text: Craft gin trade to show rise

indicators.note: to craft is to shape or fashion, so the letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A boom in artisan gin sales is shown by an upward trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like the craft-gin label but signals rearranging GINTRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, the amount by which a road or graph goes up, so it is a rise.

clue.text: Criminal Mafia boss hiding ingot under carpet

indicators.note: hiding means concealing, so the Mafia boss word holds the other pieces

parts.note: a don is a Mafia chief

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the ingot piece follows the carpet piece

parts.note: a rug is a carpet
a bar is an ingot of metal

explanation.surface: A godfather stashes a gold bar beneath a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug baron is someone who runs a large illegal narcotics trade, a criminal.

clue.text: Tip off pro: create conflict between opponents

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: between places the conflict word between the two opponents

parts.note: in bridge, East and North sit on rival sides
to war is to engage in conflict

explanation.surface: A professional is tipped to stir up trouble among rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play East-West, so E and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To forewarn is to warn in advance, the same as giving a tip-off.

clue.text: Maybe Bonnie but not Clyde getting life term

definitions.meaning: Bonnie Parker was a female gangster, a ..., while her partner Clyde Barrow was a male one
a period of life: the years of being a young female

explanation.surface: An outlaw's fate: Bonnie, unlike Clyde, is sentenced to life imprisonment.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: a hood is a gangster, and Bonnie was a female one.
explanation.definitionFit: Girlhood is the stage of life when one is a young female, a term or span of a lifetime.

clue.text: Minor injuries as goat feeds

definitions.meaning: an animal eating grass while wandering

explanation.surface: A goat picks up cuts and scratches as it eats.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazes are both slight skin abrasions and what animals do when they feed on grass.

clue.text: Announced confectionery for sets

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word for confectionery is heard rather than seen

parts.note: sweets are confectionery, sugary treats

explanation.surface: Someone declares which candies are going into the collections.
explanation.definitionFit: Suites are matching sets, such as of furniture, rooms or musical pieces.

clue.text: Content day is finally empty

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday, a day

indicators.note: empty means hollowed out, so only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: Someone is happy that the day is at last free of commitments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like an adjective but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To content someone is to please them enough, which is to satisfy.

clue.text: Pretended to eat mushroom and swallowed

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it in, so the mushroom goes inside

parts.note: to act is to pretend
a cep is an edible wild mushroom, the porcini

explanation.surface: Someone faked eating a fungus and then actually gulped it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow an idea is to believe it, and accepted means believed or taken in.

clue.text: Copper keeping home initially hampered nick

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the home word sits inside the copper

parts.note: a copper is a police constable, PC
in means at home

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A policeman detaining a householder made the arrest difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' is British slang for steal or arrest; here it means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch something is to steal it, which is British slang nick.

clue.text: Direct training after a second-rate game

indicators.note: the training abbreviation is placed after the earlier pieces

parts.note: B grade is second-rate
RU is rugby union, a game
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Exercise follows a poor game, in a straightforward account of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt or direct manner is blunt and curt, with no softening.

clue.text: Common bugs curable regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: Everyday infections can be treated in most cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual means ordinary and frequently met with, which is common.

clue.text: Vessel carrying article to north island

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so backwards
carrying means holding, so the article goes inside the vessel

parts.note: a mug is a drinking vessel
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A ship transports goods up toward an island in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Guam is an island in the western Pacific, a US territory.

clue.text: Scoffed being defeated, losing billions

indicators.note: losing means dropping, so the billions letter is taken away

parts.note: beaten means defeated
B is an abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: Someone mocked for having lost and losing a fortune too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like mocked, but it is British slang for ate greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to gobble it, so scoffed means consumed.

clue.text: Tanks being clear sign to involve leader of military

indicators.note: to involve is to include, so the leader's letter is taken in

parts.note: Aquarius is the water-bearer, a sign of the zodiac associated with clear water

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Armoured vehicles are an obvious signal that the army is getting involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanks' suggests the army, but means glass containers for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquariums are glass tanks for keeping fish and other water creatures.

clue.text: Incredibly confused laymen with no help

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Untrained people are astonishingly bewildered when given no assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' acts on LAYMEN together with NOHELP; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenally means extraordinarily or remarkably, an intensifier like incredibly.
